standalone_statement_tex:
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $r$ be a cardinal. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ has rank $r$,
\item for all $U \subset X$ nonempty affine open $\mathcal{F}(U)$
is an $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$-module of rank $r$, and
\item for some $U \subset X$ nonempty affine open $\mathcal{F}(U)$
is an $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$-module of rank $r$.
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rank-tensor}
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let
$\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The rank of $\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{G}$
is the product of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, then
the rank of $\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is the product of the ranks of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

standalone_statement_tex:
Let $X$ be an integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ has finite rank $r \geq 0$, and
\item there exists a nonempty open $U \subset X$
such that $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is free of rank $r$.
\end{enumerate}
